title: Machine learning predicts gestational diabetes from nationwide electronic health records
summary: Models trained on retrospective records of 588,622 pregnancies in Israel predicted gestational diabetes at pregnancy initiation with an auROC of 0.85 against 0.68 for a baseline risk score. Results held on a future validation set and a geographical validation set from Jerusalem, and a nine-question model reached an auROC of 0.80.
ai_technology: Machine-learning (gradient boosting) models on electronic health record data

evidence.tested: Future temporal and geographic (Jerusalem) validation sets: auROC 0.85 at pregnancy initiation versus 0.68 baseline.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective; the authors state prospective studies and other populations are needed; abstract only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning predicted risk and identified previously unreported risk factors such as earlier glucose challenge test results.
